They finished 8th in atlantic division - a final placement that frames every decision this summer. The work now runs through the draft table, the trade market and the cap sheet, and the bets made over the next few weeks will shape the roster that shows up to camp. The next headline here comes from the front office, not the scoreboard. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Jays have spent much of June looking like a club fighting its own shadow, but last night offered a cleaner picture - and a needed one. Toronto throttled Boston 6-1 behind a late burst that included George Springer's two-run homer, his 300th career blast, a milestone swing that gave the clubhouse some lift and reminded everyone that the veteran still changes games with one violent crack of the bat. The Blue Jays are 35-38, third in the AL East, 10 games back and still stuck at -1.5 in the points column, which is not the profile of a contender and not the record of a club that can waste many more soft innings. The good news is that the bats showed life in the win, with Davis Schneider and Andrés Giménez also drawing notice in the box-score glow, and the better news is that Toronto gets right back to work after snapping a rough patch that included losses of 8-3 and 3-1 to the Yankees. Now comes the test - Wednesday night in Boston at 5:45 p.m. ET, where the Jays have to prove the win was a spark, not a fluke.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Toronto Raptors have finally exhaled, their 46-36 campaign ending in the quiet aftermath of a season that promised more than it delivered. Though they finished third in the Atlantic Division, trailing by just 10 points, the final W1 streak masks a year of inconsistency and missed opportunities. The most defining moment now isn't a game result - it's the Raptors' optimistic draft strategy, revealed just days before the 2026 NBA Draft, as the team prepares to select at No. 19 despite lacking a first-round pick from a prior trade. Assistant general manager Dan Tolzman insists the club will target the best available player, regardless of position, a bold stance in an era where NIL and college realities are reshaping talent pipelines. The story right now isn't a struggling star or a breakout rookie, but the front office's quiet confidence in turning a modest draft slot into a foundational piece. With the season over and the Finals in full swing, the real battle begins in the draft room: what the Raptors build next will define their next three years.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Momentum in June is a fragile thing, but the Commanders have found one clean storyline worth pressing: Dan Quinn says Van Jefferson has stood out this offseason. That matters because this is the kind of window where roles are won, not announced - especially for a team that finished 3rd in the NFC East and 6 games back, with no margin for lazy assumptions and no room to mail in a receiver room that still needs reliable hands. Jefferson's emergence gives Washington a live competition to watch, while the chatter around Daronte Jones' scheme being easy to grasp suggests the staff wants speed of thought as much as speed of feet. Add in the buzz on an impossible-to-ignore UDFA riser, and you can see the shape of camp already: veterans being challenged, newcomers being accelerated, and every rep carrying a little more weight than it did in April. The smart money says the next weeks belong to the players who can digest the playbook fastest and separate in a crowded pack - and the real test will be whether Jefferson, the young defenders, and that surprise rookie keep forcing the coaches' hand by the start of training camp.
